quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: The Olympic Peninsula receives more rainfall than almost anywhere else in the continental United States, with some areas getting over 140 inches per year! This creates temperate rainforests where moss drapes the trees like green velvet curtains. The Hoh Rainforest, just a short drive from Port Angeles, is one of the most magical places to experience this lush wonderland.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Hummingbirds
short_read.teaser: These tiny jewels can fly backwards and their hearts beat over 1,200 times per minute! Learn about the amazing abilities of these garden visitors.

medium_read.title: The Golden Age of Hungarian Thermal Baths
medium_read.teaser: Budapest's thermal baths have been healing and delighting visitors for over 2,000 years, from Roman times through the Ottoman era to today. Discover the rich history and culture of these beautiful bathing traditions.

long_read.title: The Return of the Gray Whales
long_read.teaser: Every year, gray whales make one of the longest migrations on Earth, traveling along the Pacific Coast past the Strait of Juan de Fuca. This is the story of their incredible journey and remarkable recovery from near extinction.

port_angeles.title: Black-Tailed Deer at Hurricane Ridge
port_angeles.description: September is a wonderful time to spot the Olympic black-tailed deer at Hurricane Ridge, as they're often seen grazing in the meadows before winter arrives. These gentle creatures are unique to the Pacific Northwest and are smaller and darker than other deer species. Bring binoculars and you might see does with their nearly-grown fawns!

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird can beat its wings up to ___ times per second during normal flight.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Exactly right! Those tiny wings are a blur of motion — no wonder they hum!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! The answer is 80 beats per second — almost too fast to imagine!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: It's actually about 80 times per second — faster than we can even see! That's what creates their humming sound.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: During courtship dives, male hummingbirds can beat their wings up to 200 times per second! This incredible speed allows them to hover perfectly in place while feeding from flowers.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'grandmother'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful! Nagymama is such a sweet word — 'nagy' means big or great, and 'mama' means mother!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The answer is Nagymama! It combines 'nagy' (great) with 'mama' (mother) — a beautiful way to honor grandmothers.
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: In Hungarian families, it's also common to hear 'Nagyanya' for grandmother, while 'Anya' means mother, 'Testvér' means sibling, and 'Barát' means friend. Hungarian is unique because it's not related to most other European languages!

puzzle_3.question: What do harbor seals use their whiskers for?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Perfect! Harbor seals have super-sensitive whiskers that can detect the tiniest movements in the water, helping them hunt fish even in murky conditions!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: Actually, they use their whiskers to sense vibrations from fish swimming nearby! These sensitive whiskers help them hunt even when they can't see well.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Harbor seals are common visitors to the Strait of Juan de Fuca and can often be spotted lounging on rocks near Port Angeles. Their whiskers are so sensitive they can follow the trail of a fish that swam by 30 seconds earlier!
